title: QA: remove obsolete JET override and complete reexport allowlist
body:
Please ignore this draft until reviewed by @ChrisRackauckas.

## What changed

- Removed `jet_kwargs = (; target_defined_modules = true)` from `test/qa/qa.jl`; SciMLTesting's standard JET configuration supplies `target_modules = (pkg,)` and `mode = :typo` without the deprecated target spelling.
- Kept `api_docs_kwargs = (; rendered_ignore = NONMODULE_REEXPORTS)` intentionally. DifferentialEquations is a facade whose manual is maintained in DiffEqDocs, and SciMLTesting 2.4.1 still requires local rendered entries for reexported functions and types.
- Added `AutoDePSpecialize`, `AutoDespecialize`, `AutoRespecialize`, and `DEVerbosity` to the same compatibility render exception as the intentional reexport allowlist. This makes the check consistent at the declared SciMLTesting 2.4 minimum.
- No source behavior or test assertions were changed; no failures were suppressed.

## Verification

Current QA environment:

```text
GROUP=QA julia --startup-file=no --project=. -e 'using Pkg; Pkg.test()'
Test Summary: | Pass  Total   Time
QA/qa.jl      |   21     21  55.7s
exit 0
```

Minimum declared harness, using a temporary environment pinned to SciMLTesting 2.4.1 and the local checkout:

```text
include("test/qa/qa.jl")
Test Summary:     | Pass  Total   Time
Quality Assurance |   21     21  43.3s
exit 0
```

The before/after check was discriminating: with the four names in `reexports_allow` but absent from `rendered_ignore`, SciMLTesting 2.4.1 failed `20 passed, 1 failed` and reported those four unrendered names. With this change, the same minimum-harness run passes 21/21.

Additional local checks:

- `julia --startup-file=no -e 'using Runic; ... Runic.format_string(...; filemode=true) ...'`: passed for `test/qa/qa.jl`.
- `typos test/qa/qa.jl`: passed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- Docs build: not applicable; this repository has no `docs/make.jl` or `docs/src`. The public-doc QA check ran as part of both QA runs.

title: Drop older SciML major versions from compat
body:
**Please ignore this PR until it has been reviewed by @ChrisRackauckas.**

## What changed

Pure `[compat]` edits that **drop older major versions of SciML packages**. For each SciML dependency, only the current major remains (existing lower bound on that major is kept). No code, tests, or package version were changed.

- `Project.toml` [deps] `OrdinaryDiffEq`: `6.53, 7` → `7` (drop 6.53; current SciML major is 7)
- `Project.toml` [deps] `SciMLBase`: `2.51, 3` → `3` (drop 2.51; current SciML major is 3)

## Why

Supporting multiple SciML majors keeps untested resolver windows. The current major is the one in the General registry; older majors are dropped even when that current major is recent.

## Verification

Current majors come from JuliaRegistries/General `Versions.toml`. Not verified here: the full test suite, QA, or a live `julia-downgrade-compat` run.

title: Bump DifferentialEquations to 8.0.3 for release
body:
These packages have unreleased changes to `src`, `ext`, or `Project.toml` relative to the
tree recorded in the General registry for their current version, but the version was never
bumped — so the changes cannot be released.

| package | from | to | kind | why |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DifferentialEquations` | 8.0.2 | **8.0.3** | patch | unreleased changes to `src`/`ext`/`Project.toml` since the registered tree |

### How the versions were chosen

Patch by default. A package was promoted to a **minor** bump only where it gained public API
or a user-facing capability. For `0.y.z` packages the non-breaking slot is `z`, so those stay
in the patch position regardless of what they added.

No package in this PR needs a major bump: comparing the exported/`@public` name sets between
each package's released commit and master, **no name that the package itself defines was
removed**. The removals that do appear are blanket reexports of names owned by other packages
(e.g. `BVPJacobianAlgorithm` and `integral`, which belong to `BoundaryValueDiffEqCore`), which
SciML does not treat as documented public API.

Registration follows once this merges.

---

title: With complex variables, ImplicitEM uses a complex datatype for the time variable
body:
**Describe the bug 🐞**

Some implicit solvers for SDEs use a complex datatype for the time variable if initial condition is a complex array. When using fixed timesteps (`adaptive=false`), `newton.jl` then attempts to do
```julia
reltol = eps(eltype(dz))
```
which leads to a `MethodError`.

**Expected behavior**

If the initial condition is of `ComplexF64` datatype, use the analogous real datatype (`Float64`) for the time variable just as in the explicit solvers.

**Minimal Reproducible Example 👇**

```julia
using DifferentialEquations

L = 4;
u₀    = zeros(ComplexF64, L);

function ff!(dα,α,p,t)
  for i=1:L
    dα[i] = 0.1 + 1im * α[i]
  end
end

function gg!(dα,α,p,t)
  for i=1:L
    dα[i] = sqrt(1/2)
  end
end

prob  = SDEProblem(ff!, gg!, u₀, (0.0, 1.0));
solver = ImplicitEM(autodiff = AutoFiniteDiff());

#following leads to a compilation error: MethodError: no method matching eps(::Type{ComplexF64})
solEM = solve(prob, solver; adaptive=false, dt=0.001)

```

title: Sync package versions with the General registry
body:
Ignore until reviewed by @ChrisRackauckas.

## What this changes

| package | from | to | why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `DifferentialEquations` | 8.0.2 | 8.0.3 | unreleased changes with no version bump |


## Why

Each `to` is the next sequential version after what is currently registered in
General. Versions that skip an unregistered version are rejected by AutoMerge's
sequential version number guideline, so they can never be registered as-is;
packages with unreleased changes and no bump cannot be registered at all.

Only the top-level `version` field of each `Project.toml` is touched.

After merge, each package still needs `@JuliaRegistrator register` (with
`subdir=` where applicable).

title: Triage note: v8 re-export surface / Rodas5 are intentional (not regressions)
body:
## Context

Multiple triage passes mistook DifferentialEquations.jl v8 / OrdinaryDiffEq.jl v7 re-export narrowing for accidental breakage (missing `Euler`, `QNDF`, `DFBDF`, `DPRKN6`, SDE solvers, or `Rodas5`).

## Intended API surface (verified on current master)

### DifferentialEquations.jl v8
`using DifferentialEquations` is intentionally thin:

```julia
@reexport using SciMLBase
@reexport using OrdinaryDiffEq
```

It does **not** re-export StochasticDiffEq, DelayDiffEq, BoundaryValueDiffEq, JumpProcesses, Sundials, SteadyStateDiffEq, LinearSolve, NonlinearSolve, Optimization, etc.

Authoritative migration table: [OrdinaryDiffEq.jl NEWS.md](https://github.com/SciML/OrdinaryDiffEq.jl/blob/master/NEWS.md) (section *DifferentialEquations.jl v8: scope reduction*). README points here via the v8 Update Notice.

### OrdinaryDiffEq.jl v7 default set
`using OrdinaryDiffEq` loads only the default solver set (via OrdinaryDiffEqDefault), including:
- `DefaultODEAlgorithm`, `Tsit5`, `AutoTsit5`, `Vern6`–`Vern9`, `AutoVern*`, `Rosenbrock23`, **`Rodas5P`**, `FBDF`

**Not** in the default set (require sublibrary import):
| Solver | Sublibrary |
|---|---|
| `Euler` | `OrdinaryDiffEqLowOrderRK` |
| `QNDF`, `DFBDF` | `OrdinaryDiffEqBDF` |
| `DPRKN6` | `OrdinaryDiffEqRKN` |
| `Rodas5` (still exists) | `OrdinaryDiffEqRosenbrock` |
| SDE solvers | `StochasticDiffEq` (not part of OrdinaryDiffEq) |

### Rodas5 vs Rodas5P
- **`Rodas5` is not removed** — it lives in `OrdinaryDiffEqRosenbrock` and is tested there.
- Default umbrella exports **`Rodas5P`**, not `Rodas5`. NEWS recommends `Rodas5P` over `Rodas5` for robustness.
- Docs example in OrdinaryDiffEq mass-matrix Rosenbrock page still mentions `Rodas5()` after `using OrdinaryDiffEqRosenbrock` (via first_steps) — consistent, not a false re-export claim.

## Docs check
- No incorrect “everything is re-exported from DifferentialEquations” claim found in the package README (migration notice present) or OrdinaryDiffEq NEWS.
- Marketing bullets on the DE README still list SDEs/DDEs/etc. as part of the *suite*; that is ecosystem marketing, not a claim that `using DifferentialEquations` loads them. Acceptable as long as the v8 notice + NEWS stay prominent.

## Recommendation
Close-as-documented / use as FAQ. No code change required. Prefer linking this issue when triage agents report “Euler not defined after using DifferentialEquations”.

This issue should be ignored until reviewed by @ChrisRackauckas if any action is taken.

title: AB3 (and other multistep methods) fails to reinitialize after callback / discontinuity because `integrator.derivative_discontinuity` is reset too early
body: **Describe the bug 🐞** When using multistep solvers (like `AB3`) with a callback, the solver fails to reinitialize its history after a discontinuity. This leads to unphysical oscillations because the solver extrapolates using the pre-discontinuity history. The root cause lies in the control flow of `OrdinaryDiffEq.jl`. In `perform_step!` for `AB3ConstantCache`, there is an explicit check: ```julia if integrator.derivative_discontinuity cache.step = 1 end ``` While `integrator.derivative_discontinuity` is correctly set to `true` after the callback executes, it is inadvertently reset to `false` before reaching the next `perform_step!`. As a result, the cache reinitialization branch is never hit. **Expected behavior** `AB3` should detect the `derivative_discontinuity`, reset `cache.step = 1`, and reinitialize. **Minimal Reproducible Example 👇** ```julia using SciMLBase using OrdinaryDiffEqTsit5 using OrdinaryDiffEqAdamsBashforthMoulton using DiffEqCallbacks using Plots function f(du, u, p, t) du[1] = -u[1] end u0 = [10.0] prob = ODEProblem(f, u0, (0.0, 10.0)) condition(u, t, integrator) = t == 4 function affect!(integrator) integrator.u[1] = 10.0 end cb = DiscreteCallback(condition, affect!) sol = solve(prob, Tsit5(), callback = cb, tstops = [4.0]; adaptive = false, dt = 0.5) plot(sol, label = "Tsit5") sol2 = solve(prob, AB3(), callback = cb, tstops = [4.0]; adaptive = false, dt = 0.5) plot!(sol2, label = "AB3") ``` **Error & Stacktrace ⚠️** No explicit error or exception is thrown. **Environment (please complete the following information):** - Output of `using Pkg; title: QA: run_qa v1.6 form + ExplicitImports
body:
**Please ignore until reviewed by @ChrisRackauckas.**

Brings this repo's QA group onto the SciMLTesting 1.6 `run_qa` form with ExplicitImports enabled.

## What changed
- `test/qa/qa.jl`: replaced the hand-rolled `Aqua.test_all` + `JET.test_package` body with `run_qa(DifferentialEquations; explicit_imports = true, jet_kwargs = (; target_defined_modules = true))`. Aqua + ExplicitImports come from SciMLTesting's own deps; JET stays opt-in via `using JET`. The prior JET `target_defined_modules = true` behavior is preserved.
- `src/DifferentialEquations.jl`: made the module-level implicit imports explicit so `no_implicit_imports` passes — `using Reexport: Reexport, @reexport` plus `import SciMLBase` / `import OrdinaryDiffEq`. The two `@reexport using ...` lines are unchanged, so all re-exports remain intact.
- `test/qa/Project.toml`: `SciMLTesting` compat → `"1.6"`. Aqua kept as a direct dep (Aqua's ambiguities child-process needs it directly); JET and SafeTestsets kept (SafeTestsets is required directly by the `run_tests` folder model's `@safetestset` wrapping on Julia 1.10). ExplicitImports is transitive via SciMLTesting and is not listed.

## ExplicitImports findings
All 6 EI checks are **green** after the source fix. The only finding was `no_implicit_imports` (the bare `using Reexport` / `@reexport using SciMLBase` / `@reexport using OrdinaryDiffEq` relied on implicit module names). Since there were only 4 such names and they are easy to make explicit, they were fixed rather than `ei_broken`-tracked. No ignore-lists were needed. No `aqua_broken` / `jet_broken` / `ei_broken` markers (the prior qa.jl had none to preserve).

## Local verification (released SciMLTesting 1.6.0, Julia 1.10, clean depot)
- QA group via `GROUP=QA test/runtests.jl`: **18/18 pass**, 0 fail/error/broken.
  - Breakdown: Aqua 11, JET 1, ExplicitImports 6 (all checks pass).
- Re-export sanity + ODE solve smoke test: `ODEProblem`/`solve`/`Tsit5`/`Rodas5P`/`ReturnCode`/... all present; solve returns `ReturnCode.Success`.
- Core group via `Pkg.test()`: **17/17 pass** (confirms the `src/` change does not regress).
- Runic-clean on both changed `.jl` files.

title: Zygote Cant differentiate through `EnsembleSolution` end times when using `terminate!` callbacks
body:
**Describe the bug 🐞**

Zygote Cant differentiate through `EnsembleSolution` end times when using `terminate!` callbacks. ForwardDiff can do it okay.

**Expected behavior**

Loss function should be differentiable w.r.t to the end time T as per https://arxiv.org/abs/2011.03902.

**Minimal Reproducible Example 👇**

```julia
using Lux, Random, ComponentArrays, Statistics
using DifferentialEquations, SciMLSensitivity
using Optimization, OptimizationOptimisers
using ForwardDiff
using Zygote

D = 4
rng = Random.Xoshiro(42)
nn = Dense(D => D, tanh)
ps, st = Lux.setup(rng, nn)
ps_ca = ComponentArray(ps)

function dudt(u, θ, t)
    x = u[1:D]
    dx, _ = Lux.apply(nn, x, θ, st)
    dt_clock = sum(abs2, dx)
    return vcat(dx, dt_clock)
end

# Terminate when the clock component >= 0.5
function condition(u, t, integrator)
    return 0.5f0 - u[D + 1]
end
cb = ContinuousCallback(condition, terminate!; save_positions = (false, true))

# Batch of 4 samples
B = 4
x = randn(rng, Float32, D, B)
y = randn(rng, Float32, D, B)

# Build u0 batch: [x; 0] for each sample (clock starts at 0)
u0_batch = vcat(x, zeros(Float32, 1, B))

ff = ODEFunction{false}(dudt)
tspan = (0.0f0, 1.0f0)

println("Testing backward passs...")

function prob_func(prob, ctx)
    remake(prob; u0 = u0_batch[:, ctx.sim_id])
end

function loss(θ)
    base_prob = ODEProblem{false}(ff, u0_batch[:, 1], tspan, θ)
    ensemble_prob = EnsembleProblem(base_prob; prob_func = prob_func, safetycopy = false)

    ensemble_sol = solve(ensemble_prob, Tsit5(), EnsembleThreads();
        sensealg = GaussAdjoint(autojacvec = ReverseDiffVJP()),
        callback = cb,
        trajectories = B
    )
    # extract end times
    T_stars = [sol.t[end] for sol in ensemble_sol.u]
    return mean(T_stars)  # Dummy loss: mean of halting times
end

gf = ForwardDiff.gradient(loss, ps_ca)
println("ForwardDiff gradient computed! values = $(gf)")
# here is where the error occurs
g = Zygote.gradient(loss, ps_ca)
println("Zygote gradient computed! values = $(g)")
```

**Error & Stacktrace ⚠️**

```julia
ERROR: LoadError: MethodError: no method matching ndims(::@NamedTuple{…})
The function `ndims` exists, but no method is defined for this combination of argument types.

Closest candidates are:
  ndims(::Type{Union{}}, Any...)
   @ Base abstractarray.jl:276
  ndims(::Type{<:AbstractChar})
   @ Base char.jl:197
  ndims(::Type{<:Ref})
   @ Base refpointer.jl:102
  ...

title: indexing error in VectorContinuousCallback
body:
**Describe the bug 🐞**

I have been using `VectorContinuousCallback()` to remove species that fall below an extinction threshold. This was working fine until I updated some packages a couple of days ago, including `DifferentialEquations.jl`. Now I am getting a BoundsError:


**Minimal Reproducible Example 👇**
```julia
using DifferentialEquations

r     = [ 1.0,   0.5]
K     = [70.0, 125.0] 
u0    = [ 5.0,   5.0]
alpha = [ 0.5,   0.5]
tspan = (0.0, 200.0) 

function condition(out, u, t, integrator)
        out .= u .- 4.
end
function affect!(integrator, i)
        integrator.u[i] = 0.0
end
extinction_cb = VectorContinuousCallback(condition,affect!, 2)

function compete!(du, u, p, t)
    N1, N2 = u
    K1 = K[1] +  5 * sin(2π * t / 100)
    K2 = K[2] - 10 * sin(2π * t / 100)
    du[1] = r[1] * N1 * (1 - (N1 + alpha[1] * N2) / K1)
    du[2] = r[2] * N2 * (1 - (N2 + alpha[2] * N1) / K2)
end

prob = ODEProblem(compete!, u0, tspan, callback = extinction_cb)
sol = solve(prob, Tsit5(), saveat = 1)
```

title: Canonicalize tests to @safetestset for module isolation
body:
## Summary

Canonicalizes `test/runtests.jl` so each independent test unit runs in its own module via `@safetestset`, matching the canonical OrdinaryDiffEq structure (isolation between tests + world-age safety).

### Classification
PLAIN-TESTSET: the suite was a single outer `@testset "DifferentialEquations"` wrapping 8 independent inner plain `@testset` units, all sharing only the top-level `using DifferentialEquations, Test, SafeTestsets`.

### What changed
- Each inner `@testset "X" begin ... end` -> `@safetestset "X" begin ... end`.
- Each `@safetestset` body is made self-contained with its own `using DifferentialEquations, Test`.
- The outer `@testset "DifferentialEquations"` wrapper and the `@time begin ... end` block are kept, so the grouped test summary is preserved (`@safetestset` nests fine inside `@testset`).

### What did NOT change
- No test logic or assertions changed. The same 17 assertions run.
- These bodies use no package macros and only resolve package symbols (`ODEProblem`, `Tsit5`, `solve`, ...) at runtime, so an inline `@safetestset` body with `using DifferentialEquations, Test` is sufficient (no `include()` indirection needed).
- `SafeTestsets` was already in `[extras]` + `[targets].test`, so `Project.toml` is unchanged.

### Verification
Ran locally with `julia +1.11` `Pkg.test()`:
```
Test Summary:         | Pass  Total   Time
DifferentialEquations |   17     17  22.3s
     Testing DifferentialEquations tests passed
```

title: Uncaught exceptions complicate the API
body:
Thanks for your excellent work on creating and maintaining this package!  Truly admirable!

I incorporate differential equations solvers from **DifferentialEquations.jl** in packages I write.  In particular, in [**PartiallyObservedMarkovProcesses.jl**](https://github.com/kingaa/PartiallyObservedMarkovProcesses.jl), I have a trajectory matching facility which, when furnished a differential equation and some data, generates an objective function that computes the mismatch between the model prediction and the data.  The user is allowed to specify not only the model and the data, but to choose from among the many integration algorithms provided by **DifferentialEquations.jl**.  Because this is meant to be fairly general, I have to allow, for example, for cases when an exception arises due to a bad (misspecified) model and also for the case when one arises in a good model at a bad point in parameter space, for example due to numerical instability at extreme values of a parameter.  In the former case, the user should be informed right away; in the latter case, one usually wants to let the optimization proceed in its search of the parameter space.

To the extent that the **DifferentialEquations.jl** API is uniform, it greatly facilitates this use.  In particular, having integrated the equations, I can examine the return code and decide whether to report the mismatch (if the integration has been successful) or return a large or infinite value (if it has not).  

This handling is frustrated by uncaught exceptions arising inside the **DifferentialEquations.jl** codes and/or in packages upon which these depend.  When such exceptions arise, it seems I have no sure way of understanding what the difficulty is and whether, in particular, I ought to catch the exception, return a large or infinite objective function value so that the optimization can proceed, or whether the error signals a fatal flaw. 

For example, a `LinearAlgebra.SingularException` tells me that some matrix computed as part of the integration algorithm is singular, but since I can't know what the user's equation is, nor which integration algorithm they've opted for, it's difficult to know where or why this has happened.

It seems to me that it would be very useful were **DifferentialEquations.jl** to itself catch exceptions that arise in its internal workings, and pass them on either (preferably) via an unsuccessful return code, or (if necessary) via an exception that contains information about what the exception signifies *in the context of the differential equation integration*.

Absent this, my options to be either (1) maintain a whitelist of exceptions that I know signal nothing worse than bad parameters and only halt operation when an exception not on that list is thrown, (2) maintain a blacklist of exceptions that I know should halt operations, or (3) punt the whole problem to the user.  Obviously, none of these is very attractive.

1. Do you agree that streamlining the API in this way would be A Good Thing?
2. How much work would it be to catch exceptions in this way within **DifferentialEquations.jl**?
3. If the answer to the first question is "no" or to the second one is "way too much", do you have advice for me?

Thanks for taking the time to think about this.

title: Canonical CI: grouped-tests.yml + root test/test_groups.toml
body:
## Summary

Converts the root test workflow to the canonical **thin caller** pattern: `SciML/.github/.github/workflows/grouped-tests.yml@v1`, with the group × version matrix declared once in a root `test/test_groups.toml`.

### Changes
- **`.github/workflows/Tests.yml`** — replaced the hand-maintained version matrix job with the thin `grouped-tests.yml@v1` caller. `on:` and `concurrency:` preserved verbatim; filename and `name:` unchanged. Linux-only (no `os` field). All inputs left at their defaults (default `GROUP` env, `check-bounds: yes`, coverage on `src,ext`).
- **`test/test_groups.toml`** (new) — the matrix:
  - `[Core]` → `["lts", "1", "pre"]`
  - `[QA]` → `["lts", "1"]`
- **`test/runtests.jl`** — added `GROUP` dispatch (`const GROUP = get(ENV, "GROUP", "All")`). The existing suite runs under `Core`/`All`; the `QA` group activates the isolated qa env and includes `qa.jl`.
- **`test/qa/Project.toml`** + **`test/qa/qa.jl`** (new) — isolated QA environment running `Aqua.test_all(DifferentialEquations)` and `JET.test_package(DifferentialEquations; target_defined_modules = true)`. Package wired via `[sources] path = "../.."`.
- **`Project.toml`** — added `[compat]` entries for the `[extras]` test deps (`Random = "1"`, `SafeTestsets = "0.1"`, `Test = "1"`). `julia` compat already at the `1.10` LTS floor (unchanged).

### Matrix match
The reusable workflow computes its matrix from `test/test_groups.toml` via `compute_affected_sublibraries.jl --root-matrix`. Verified statically (Julia 1.11, no tests run):

```
Core × {lts, 1, pre}  on ubuntu-latest
QA   × {lts, 1}        on ubuntu-latest
```

The old `Tests.yml` matrix was a single implicit "all tests" group on `{1, lts, pre}` (Linux). The new **Core** group reproduces that exactly; **QA** is purely additive.

### Verification (static only)
- `compute_affected_sublibraries.jl --root-matrix` reproduces the expected (group, version, runner) set.
- TOML (root `Project.toml`, `test_groups.toml`, `qa/Project.toml`) and YAML (`Tests.yml`) parse cleanly.
- `runtests.jl` and `qa/qa.jl` parse as valid Julia.
- No tests / Aqua / JET were run locally — this is a structural conversion.

### Notes
QA group is **newly wired**; Aqua/JET run in CI — any failures will be triaged in a follow-up. No test or Aqua/JET exclusions were added.

body:

Converts the remaining inline CI workflows to the centralized `SciML/.github` reusable workflow callers (all pinned `@v1`, every caller gets `secrets: "inherit"`). Matches the Sundials.jl end-state.

## Converted (inline -> central)
- **FormatCheck.yml**: inline `fredrikekre/runic-action` -> `runic.yml@v1`
- **SpellCheck.yml**: inline `crate-ci/typos@v1.18.0` -> `spellcheck.yml@v1`
- **Downgrade.yml**: inline `julia-actions/julia-downgrade-compat` -> `downgrade.yml@v1` (preserves `julia-version: 1.10`, `skip: Pkg,TOML`, `allow-reresolve: false`)

## Unchanged
- **Tests.yml**: already a `tests.yml@v1` caller with `secrets: "inherit"` and the `1`/`lts`/`pre` version matrix — left exactly as-is.
- **TagBot.yml**: unchanged.

## Added callers
- None. The repo already had Tests, Runic (FormatCheck), SpellCheck, and Downgrade. No `docs/` dir, so no Documentation caller. No existing Downstream/Benchmark/CompatHelper workflows.

## Other changes
- **dependabot.yml**: removed the `crate-ci/typos` version-update ignore (typos version is now pinned/managed by the central spellcheck workflow). The `github-actions` (weekly, `/`) and `julia` (daily, group `all-julia-packages: ["*"]`, dirs `/` and `/test`) blocks are preserved.

## Checks
- Typos: ran `typos .` -> exit 0 (clean), no changes needed. Existing `.typos.toml` preserved.
- Runic: installed Runic v1.7.0 and ran `--inplace .` -> no formatting changes (repo was already Runic-clean from the prior inline check).
- All changed YAML validated with `yaml.safe_load`.

## Note on branch protection
The job/check names change when moving to reusable workflows (e.g. `runic` -> the reusable workflow's `Runic Format Check`, `typos-check` -> `Spell Check with Typos`, Downgrade `test` -> `Downgrade Tests`). Required status checks in branch protection will need to be updated to the new names.

Bumps [julia-actions/setup-julia](https://github.com/julia-actions/setup-julia) from 2 to 3.
Release notes

Sourced from julia-actions/setup-julia's releases.

v3.0.0

:warning: Breaking Changes, and Migration Guide for v2 ⟶ v3

  1. v3 requires Node 24 (compared to v2, which required Node 20).
  2. The behavior of version: min has changed between v2 and v3.
    • In v2, version: min would resolve to the minimum major/minor/patch, e.g. 1.10.0.
    • In v3, version: min resolves to the minimum major/minor but the latest patch, e.g. 1.10.11.
    • If you specifically want the minimum major/minor/patch under v3, you should specify version: min-patch. Note: v3 also adds the alias version: min-minor, which is equivalent to version: min.
  3. v3 will throw an error if x86_64 Julia binaries are requested on Apple Silicon macOS. (Under v2, this was a warning.) Under v3, if you specifically want to run x86_64 Julia binaries on Apple Silicon (under Rosetta 2), you must now opt-in by specifying the force-arch: true input.

Other Changes

We updated some dependencies, and we improved and updated the CI tooling on this repo.

Release notes

Sourced from julia-actions/setup-julia's releases.

v3.0.0

:warning: Breaking Changes, and Migration Guide for v2 ⟶ v3

  1. v3 requires Node 24 (compared to v2, which required Node 20).
  2. The behavior of version: min has changed between v2 and v3.
    • In v2, version: min would resolve to the minimum major/minor/patch, e.g. 1.10.0.
    • In v3, version: min resolves to the minimum major/minor but the latest patch, e.g. 1.10.11.
    • If you specifically want the minimum major/minor/patch under v3, you should specify version: min-patch. Note: v3 also adds the alias version: min-minor, which is equivalent to version: min.
  3. v3 will throw an error if x86_64 Julia binaries are requested on Apple Silicon macOS. (Under v2, this was a warning.) Under v3, if you specifically want to run x86_64 Julia binaries on Apple Silicon (under Rosetta 2), you must now opt-in by specifying the force-arch: true input.

Other Changes

We updated some dependencies, and we improved and updated the CI tooling on this repo.

body:
Updates the requirements on [SciMLBase](https://github.com/SciML/SciMLBase.jl) to permit the latest version. Updates `SciMLBase` to 3.0.0
Release notes

Sourced from SciMLBase's releases.

v3.0.0

SciMLBase v3.0.0

Diff since v2.154.0

SciMLBase v3.0.0 — Breaking Release

RecursiveArrayTools v4: Solution types are now AbstractArrays (#1297)

Most impactful change. AbstractVectorOfArray (and thus ODESolution, DDESolution, RODESolution, DAESolution) now subtypes AbstractArray:

  • sol[i] returns the ith scalar element (column-major), not the ith timestep. Use sol.u[i] or sol[:, i] for timesteps.
  • length(sol) returns total elements (prod(size(sol))). Use length(sol.u) for number of timesteps.
  • iterate(sol) iterates scalar elements. Use sol.u for timestep iteration.
  • map(f, sol) maps over elements. Use map(f, sol.u) for timesteps.

Ensemble RNG redesign (#1252)

  • prob_func(prob, i, repeat) → prob_func(prob, ctx) where ctx::EnsembleContext
  • output_func(sol, i) → output_func(sol, ctx)
  • EnsembleContext includes sim_id, repeat, rng, sim_seed, worker_id, master_rng
  • New seed/rng/rng_func kwargs on solve() for deterministic, thread-count-independent ensemble solves

Removed deprecated APIs

  • u_modified! renamed to derivative_discontinuity! (#1289)
  • Removed deprecated.jl: old type aliases (DEAlgorithm, DEProblem, DESolution, etc.), constructors, deprecated accessors (#1291)
  • Removed backward compat shims in remake.jl and MLStyle extension (#1292)
  • Removed old iterators: tuples, intervals, TimeChoiceIterator (#1290)

Simplified getproperty

  • Removed redundant getproperty overloads on solution abstract types (#1293)
  • Removed deprecated getproperty aliases (.destats, .x, .lb/.ub, .minimizer, .minimum) (#1294)

Other breaking changes

  • Replaced Moshi with plain Julia structs for Clocks — 23% precompilation improvement (#1295)
  • ODEFunction uses DEFAULT_SPECIALIZATION (AutoSpecialize) for convenience constructors (#1300)
  • Propagate interp/dense to DiffEqArrays from solution callables (#1297)
  • is_discrete_time_domain(nothing) now returns false (#1306)

Migration Guide

Old (v2) New (v3)
sol[i] (timestep) sol.u[i] or sol[:, i]
length(sol) (timesteps) length(sol.u)
for u in sol for u in sol.u
u_modified!(integrator, true) derivative_discontinuity!(integrator, true)
prob_func(prob, i, repeat) prob_func(prob, ctx) — use ctx.sim_id, ctx.repeat
output_func(sol, i) output_func(sol, ctx)
sol.destats sol.stats

title: improve argument validation in "solve" function
body:
The issue arose when trying to use solve with an EnsembleProblem on the GPU.

Using the positional arguments otherwise, but ensemblealg as a kwarg made the function default back to CPU instead of GPU, masking the fact that the solver I was using was not fit for the GPU, and debugging of my function call harder.


It would be more friendly to the user if at least passing a positional arg as a kwarg threw a warning or error,  making it visible to the user that they're misusing the function.

title: Mutation attempt in `ContinuousCallback` when solving `SDEProblem{StaticArraysCore.SVector}`
body:
**Describe the bug 🐞**

When solving an `SDEProblem` with an `SVector` state and a `ContinuousCallback`, `sde_interpolant!` is called and there is a mutation attempt on the `SVector` raising an error. This does not occur when solving the equivalent `ODEProblem`.

**Expected behavior**

When applying the callback `apply_callback!`, the interpolant should be non-mutating, like in the ODE case.

**Minimal Reproducible Example 👇**

```julia
import DifferentialEquations as DE
import StaticArrays as SA

function f(u::V, p, t) where V <: SA.StaticVector
    V(u[2], -p)
end
function g(::V, p, t) where V <: SA.StaticVector
    V(1., 0.)
end

function condition(u, t, integrator)
    u[1]
end

cb = DE.ContinuousCallback(condition, DE.terminate!)

u0 = SA.SVector(1., 0.)
tspan = (0.0, 1.)
p = 4.

## SDE out-of-place
fn = DE.SDEFunction{false}(f, g)
sdeprob = DE.SDEProblem(fn, u0, tspan, p)

DE.solve(sdeprob, DE.SOSRI()) # retcode: Success
DE.solve(sdeprob, DE.SOSRI(); callback = cb) # setindex!(::StaticArraysCore.SVector{2, Float64}, value, ::Int) is not defined
```

title: Reducing stack trace length by specializing structs for common type combinations (VF64 pattern)
body:
## Problem

Julia's parametric type system propagates type parameters through the entire struct hierarchy. When a user calls `solve(prob)` on a simple ODE problem, the resulting integrator and solution types carry **tens of thousands of characters** in their type strings. These appear in:

- Stack traces during errors (the primary user-facing problem)
- `@code_warntype` output
- IDE hover tooltips
- REPL display of types

For the default `solve(ODEProblem(f!, u0, tspan))` path, the **original** `ODEIntegrator` type was approximately **80,000+ characters**. Stack traces from a simple `solve` call would be nearly unreadable.

## Solution: The VF64 Pattern

PR [SciML/OrdinaryDiffEq.jl#3058](https://github.com/SciML/OrdinaryDiffEq.jl/pull/3058) implements a systematic approach to reducing type parameter counts by creating **specialized struct variants** for the most common type combination: **in-place `Vector{Float64}` problems with default options**.

The key insight: most fields in ODE solver caches are typed with generic parameters like `uType`, `rateType`, `tType`, but for the overwhelmingly common case of `u::Vector{Float64}`, these are always `Vector{Float64}`, `Float64`, `Matrix{Float64}`, etc. By creating a parallel struct that hardcodes these concrete types, we eliminate the type parameters entirely.

### Pattern: Generic struct → VF64 specialized struct

**Before** (generic, 10 type params):
```julia
mutable struct NLNewtonCache{uType, tType, tType2, rateType, J, W, ufType, jcType, lsType} <: AbstractNLSolverCache
    ustep::uType
    tstep::tType
    k::rateType
    atmp::uType
    dz::uType
    J::J
    W::W
    new_W::Bool
    du1::uType
    uf::ufType
    jac_config::jcType
    linsolve::lsType
    weight::uType
    invγdt::tType2
    # ...
end
```

**After** (VF64 specialized, 2-3 type params):
```julia
mutable struct NLNewtonCacheVF64{pType, LSType, JCType} <: AbstractNLSolverCache
    ustep::Vector{Float64}
    tstep::Float64
    k::Vector{Float64}
    atmp::Vector{Float64}
    dz::Vector{Float64}
    J::Matrix{Float64}
    W::Matrix{Float64}
    new_W::Bool
    du1::Vector{Float64}
    uf::OrdinaryDiffEqCore._UJacobianWrapperVF64Type{pType}
    jac_config::JCType
    linsolve::LSType
    weight::Vector{Float64}
    invγdt::Float64
    # ...
end
```

### Pattern: Union-based dispatch for backward compatibility

The critical pattern for maintaining dispatch is defining a union type:

```julia
const NLNewtonCacheType = Union{NLNewtonCache, NLNewtonCacheVF64, NLNewtonCacheVF64FiniteDiff}
```

Then all methods that previously dispatched on `NLNewtonCache` dispatch on `NLNewtonCacheType` instead. Since both structs have identical field names, all field access works unchanged. The only change is in the constructor, which branches based on the problem type:

```julia
if u isa Vector{Float64} && prob.f isa _ODEFunctionVF64Type
    # Construct VF64 variant
else
    # Construct generic variant (original behavior)
end
```

### Pattern: Type aliases for complex nested types

Many type parameters can't be fully eliminated but can be shortened using `const` type aliases that absorb common sub-types:

```julia
# Instead of ODEFunction{true, AutoSpecialize, FunctionWrappersWrapper{...}, ...} appearing everywhere:
const _ODEFunctionVF64Type{P} = SciMLBase.ODEFunction{
    true, SciMLBase.AutoSpecialize,
    _ODEFunctionWrapperType{P},
    UniformScaling{Bool},
    Nothing, Nothing, Nothing, Nothing, Nothing, Nothing, Nothing, Nothing, Nothing,
    Nothing, Nothing,
    typeof(SciMLBase.DEFAULT_OBSERVED),
    Nothing, Nothing, Nothing, Nothing,
}
```

This allows downstream structs to use `_ODEFunctionVF64Type{pType}` (parameterized only by `P`) instead of carrying the full 20-parameter ODEFunction type.

### Pattern: Hardcoding AD-backend-specific prep types

When the autodiff backend determines a concrete prep type that is **function-independent**, that type can be computed once at module load time and hardcoded:

```julia
# FiniteDiff jacobian preps are function-independent
let
    _du = zeros(2); _u = zeros(2)
    _uf_dummy = (y, x) -> nothing
    _fd_fwd = DI.prepare_jacobian(_uf_dummy, _du, AutoFiniteDiff(; dir = 1), _u, strict = Val(false))
    _fd_rev = DI.prepare_jacobian(_uf_dummy, _du, AutoFiniteDiff(; dir = -1), _u, strict = Val(false))
    global const _JacConfigFiniteDiff = Tuple{typeof(_fd_fwd), typeof(_fd_rev)}
end

# Then in the struct:
mutable struct NLNewtonCacheVF64FiniteDiff{pType, LSType} <: AbstractNLSolverCache
    # ...
    jac_config::_JacConfigFiniteDiff  # hardcoded, no type parameter needed
    # ...
end
```

**Important caveat**: This only works when the prep type doesn't encode the function type. Testing revealed:
- **FiniteDiff jacobian preps**: function-independent (can hardcode)
- **ForwardDiff jacobian preps**: encodes `ForwardDiff.Tag{F}` with function type + chunk size (CANNOT hardcode)
- **FiniteDiff derivative preps**: encodes function type (CANNOT hardcode)
- **ForwardDiff derivative preps**: encodes `ForwardDiff.Tag{F}` (CANNOT hardcode)

## Results

### Structs created in OrdinaryDiffEq.jl#3058

| Original Struct | VF64 Variant | Params reduced |
|----------------|-------------|---------------|
| `ODEIntegrator{22 params}` | `ODEIntegratorVF64{4 params}` | 22 → 4 |
| `ODESolution{16 params}` | `ODESolutionVF64{3 params}` | 16 → 3 |
| `InterpolationData{7 params}` | `InterpolationDataVF64{2 params}` | 7 → 2 |
| `DefaultCache{11 params}` | `DefaultCacheVF64{7 params}` | 11 → 7 |
| `Rosenbrock23Cache{17 params}` | `Rosenbrock23CacheVF64FiniteDiff{5 params}` | 17 → 5 |
| `RosenbrockCache{21 params}` | `RosenbrockCacheVF64FiniteDiff{5 params}` | 21 → 5 |
| `NLNewtonCache{10 params}` | `NLNewtonCacheVF64FiniteDiff{2 params}` | 10 → 2 |
| `NLSolver{8 params}` | `NLSolverVF64{2 params}` | 8 → 2 |
| `FBDFCache{21 params}` | `FBDFCacheVF64{3 params}` | 21 → 3 |
| `Tsit5Cache{10 params}` | `Tsit5CacheVF64{0 params}` | 10 → 0 |
| `Vern7Cache{14 params}` | `Vern7CacheVF64{0 params}` | 14 → 0 |

### Character count breakdown (default `solve(prob)` path)

The `DefaultCacheVF64` type string is now **14,978 chars** (down from 80,000+). Here's where the remaining characters come from:

```
DefaultCacheVF64{7 params} ........................... 14,978 (100%)
├─ Tsit5CacheVF64 .....................................    34  (0.2%)
├─ Vern7CacheVF64 .....................................    35  (0.2%)
├─ Rosenbrock23CacheVF64FiniteDiff{5 params} ......... 5,568 (37.2%)
│  ├─ pType (NullParameters) ..........................    24  (0.2%)
│  ├─ AlgType (Rosenbrock23{9}) .......................   308  (2.1%)
│  ├─ TabType ........................................     53  (0.4%)
│  ├─ LSType (LinearCache{12}) ....................... 1,592 (10.6%)
│  │  ├─ DefaultLinearSolverInit{25 factorizations} ..   899  (6.0%)
│  │  └─ LinearVerbosity{16 log levels} ..............   369  (2.5%)
│  └─ GCType (grad_config: Tuple of 2 preps) ........ 3,525 (23.5%)
│     └─ FiniteDiffTwoArgDerivativePrep × 2 ......... 3,516
│        └─ TimeGradientWrapper × 2 ................. 2,818
│           └─ ODEFunction{20 params} ............... 1,329
│              └─ FunctionWrappersWrapper ........... 1,077
│                 └─ 4× FunctionWrapper{ForwardDiff.Dual...}
├─ RosenbrockCacheVF64FiniteDiff{5 params} ........... 5,563 (37.1%)
│  └─ (identical structure to Rosenbrock23 above)
├─ FBDFCacheVF64{3 params} ........................... 1,907 (12.7%)
│  └─ NLSolverVF64{2 params} ........................ 1,818
│     └─ NLNewtonCacheVF64FiniteDiff{2 params} ...... 1,676
│        └─ LSType (LinearCache) .................... 1,592
├─ Union{} ...........................................      7  (0.0%)
└─ AutoSwitchCache{4 params} ......................... 1,815 (12.1%)
   ├─ stiff alg tuple (4 algs) ...................... 1,474
   └─ non-stiff alg tuple (2 algs) ..................   279
```

### Biggest remaining repeated components

| Component | Chars each | Instances | Total chars | % of 14,978 |
|-----------|----------:|----------:|------------:|------------|
| **LinearCache** | 1,592 | 4 | ~6,368 | 42.5% |
| └ DefaultLinearSolverInit | 899 | 4 | 3,596 | 24.0% |
| └ LinearVerbosity | 369 | 4 | 1,476 | 9.9% |
| **GCType (grad_config)** | 3,525 | 2 | 7,050 | 47.1% |
| └ TimeGradientWrapper | 1,409 | 4 | 5,636 | 37.6% |
| └ ODEFunction | 1,329 | 4 | 5,316 | 35.5% |
| └ FunctionWrappersWrapper | 1,077 | 4 | 4,308 | 28.8% |

## Key Learnings

1. **Union-based dispatch is the right pattern.** Defining `const MyType = Union{OriginalStruct, VF64Struct}` and dispatching on the union means all existing methods work without modification. Field names must match between the variants.

2. **Start from the innermost caches and work outward.** Each level's VF64 variant reduces the type parameters at the next level up. Tsit5CacheVF64 (0 params) appears as a single token in DefaultCacheVF64, versus Tsit5Cache{10 params} which would expand to hundreds of characters.

3. **Not all type parameters can be eliminated.** Some types genuinely vary at runtime or encode function-specific information. The remaining params in VF64 structs (like `pType`, `AlgType`, `LSType`, `GCType`) can't be hardcoded because they depend on user choices (parameter type, linear solver, AD backend).

4. **ForwardDiff prep types encode function identity.** `ForwardDiff.Tag{F, V}` bakes the function type `F` into every prep, making it impossible to hardcode the prep type without knowing the function at module load time. FiniteDiff jacobian preps do NOT have this issue.

5. **`FunctionWrappersWrapper` propagates through everything.** The 4 FunctionWrapper types (1,077 chars) encoding the ForwardDiff dual call signatures appear in every ODEFunction, which appears in every TimeGradientWrapper, which appears in every grad_config. This is the deepest source of type string bloat and comes from SciMLBase's function wrapping system.

6. **LinearSolve.jl's `LinearCache` is the biggest single upstream contributor.** At 1,592 chars per instance and 4 instances in the default path, it accounts for 42.5% of the remaining type string. The two biggest sub-components are:
   - `DefaultLinearSolverInit` (899 chars): stores 25 pre-allocated matrix factorization slots (LU, QR, SVD, Cholesky, etc.), 13 of which are `Nothing`
   - `LinearVerbosity` (369 chars): 16 separate `SciMLLogging.Silent`/`WarnLevel` type parameters for log categories

## Future Work / Opportunities in Other Packages

### LinearSolve.jl

**`DefaultLinearSolverInit` (899 chars, 25 params)** — This stores every possible dense matrix factorization pre-allocated. For the VF64 default path, this is always the same concrete type. A VF64-specialized `LinearCacheVF64` that hardcodes `DefaultLinearSolverInit` and `LinearVerbosity` could save ~1,268 chars per instance (× 4 instances = ~5,072 chars, 34% of the total).

**`LinearVerbosity` (369 chars, 16 params)** — 16 type parameters for log levels that are almost always `Silent`. Could be replaced with a concrete default type alias.

### SciMLBase.jl / FunctionWrappersWrappers

**`FunctionWrappersWrapper` (1,077 chars)** — The 4 FunctionWrapper instances carry `ForwardDiff.Dual{Tag{OrdinaryDiffEqTag}}` in their argument types. This is baked in at `ODEProblem` construction time. Opportunities:
- Create a type alias `const _DefaultFunctionWrappersWrapper = FunctionWrappersWrapper{...}` for the common case
- Consider whether FunctionWrappersWrapper could avoid encoding the dual types explicitly

### DifferentiationInterface.jl

**FiniteDiff derivative preps (1,758 chars each)** encode the function type (`TimeGradientWrapper{ODEFunction{FunctionWrappersWrapper{...}}}`). If DI preps could be made function-type-independent (similar to how `strict=Val(false)` strips the signature but not the function type), this would eliminate the `GCType` parameter entirely from Rosenbrock caches, saving 3,525 chars × 2 = 7,050 chars (47% of the total).

### Applying this pattern to other SciML packages

Any package with deeply nested parametric types can benefit from this pattern. The recipe:

1. **Identify the most common concrete type combination** (e.g., `Vector{Float64}` for ODE solvers)
2. **Create VF64 (or similar) struct variants** that hardcode the common fields
3. **Define union types** for dispatch: `const MyTypeUnion = Union{MyType, MyTypeVF64}`
4. **Update all dispatch** to use the union type
5. **Branch in the constructor** based on whether the inputs match the specialized path
6. **Add `full_cache`, `get_fsalfirstlast`**, and any other accessor methods for the new variants
7. **Test**: all existing tests should pass without modification since the union dispatch is transparent

Candidates for this treatment in the SciML ecosystem:
- **NonlinearSolve.jl** — Newton solver caches
- **StochasticDiffEq.jl** — SDE solver caches
- **DelayDiffEq.jl** — DDE integrator/caches
- **BoundaryValueDiffEq.jl** — BVP solver caches
- Any package that stores `LinearCache`, `ODEFunction`, or DI preps as type parameters

## Reference Implementation

The full implementation is in [SciML/OrdinaryDiffEq.jl#3058](https://github.com/SciML/OrdinaryDiffEq.jl/pull/3058) on branch `reduce-integrator-type-params` at `ChrisRackauckas-Claude/OrdinaryDiffEq.jl`. Key files:

- **Type aliases**: `lib/OrdinaryDiffEqCore/src/integrators/type_vf64.jl`
- **FiniteDiff prep type computation**: `lib/OrdinaryDiffEqDifferentiation/src/vf64_prep_types.jl`
- **VF64 cache structs**: `lib/OrdinaryDiffEqNonlinearSolve/src/type.jl`, `lib/OrdinaryDiffEqRosenbrock/src/rosenbrock_caches.jl`
- **Constructor branching**: `lib/OrdinaryDiffEqNonlinearSolve/src/utils.jl`, `lib/OrdinaryDiffEqRosenbrock/src/rosenbrock_caches.jl`
- **DefaultCache VF64**: `lib/OrdinaryDiffEqCore/src/caches/basic_caches.jl`
- **Integrator/Solution VF64**: `lib/OrdinaryDiffEqCore/src/integrators/type_vf64.jl`

title: DAE initialization should be triggered by u_modified!
body:
**Describe the bug 🐞*

Perturbing the state of a DAE integrator (described with `u_modified!`) does not call `integrator.initializealg`
even through this does happen when the state is changed through a callback.

**Expected behavior**

The state should be initialized if `integrator.u_modified == true`, or another way to manually call the initialization algorithm.

**Minimal Reproducible Example 👇**

```julia
using DifferentialEquations

function f(out, du, u, _, _)
    out[1] = -0.04u[1] + 1e4 * u[2] * u[3] - du[1]
    out[2] = +0.04u[1] - 3e7 * u[2]^2 - 1e4 * u[2] * u[3] - du[2]
    out[3] = u[1] + u[2] + u[3] - 1.0
end

u₀ = [1.0, 0, 0]
du₀ = [-0.04, 0.04, 0.0]

prob = DAEProblem(f, du₀, u₀, (0.0, 1.0), differential_vars = [true, true, false])

println("With integrator interface (u_modified!)")
int = init(prob, DFBDF(), initializealg = DiffEqBase.CheckInit())
int.u[1] = 2.0 # Breaks algebraic constraints
u_modified!(int, true)
step!(int) # Step accepted even through constraints are violated
@show int.u # u[3] has been changed to satisfy constraints

println("\nWith a callback")
condition(u, t, integrator) = true
affect!(integrator) = integrator.u[1] = 2.0 # Breaks algebraic constraints
cb = DiscreteCallback(condition, affect!)
int = init(prob, DFBDF(), initializealg = DiffEqBase.CheckInit(), callback = cb)
step!(int) # Step rejected due to constraints being violated
```

title: Fix deprecation warnings
body:
## Summary

- Replace the trivial `@test true` test suite with comprehensive tests that exercise core re-exported functionality (scalar ODE, in-place ODE, stiff ODE, interpolation, callbacks, remake, saveat)
- All tests use non-deprecated API patterns — specifically `sol.u[i]` instead of the deprecated `sol[i]` integer indexing from RecursiveArrayTools
- All 17 tests pass with `JULIA_DEPWARN=error`

## Upstream deprecation notes

**RecursiveArrayTools.jl** (v3.47.0): `sol[i]` (integer indexing on `AbstractDiffEqArray`) is deprecated in favor of `sol.u[i]`. This is an upstream deprecation that does not affect DifferentialEquations.jl's own code, but users should migrate their code accordingly. The `sol[i,:]` and `sol[:,i]` component/timestep indexing patterns remain non-deprecated.

## Investigation process

1. Cloned repo and ran `JULIA_DEPWARN=error julia --project -e 'using Pkg; Pkg.test()'` — tests pass trivially (was just `@test true`)
2. Tested `using DifferentialEquations` with `--depwarn=error` — no deprecation warnings during loading or precompilation
3. Systematically tested common API patterns (ODE construction, solving, solution access, interpolation, callbacks, remake, saveat) with `--depwarn=error`
4. Identified that `sol[i]` integer indexing is deprecated in RecursiveArrayTools (upstream)
5. Wrote comprehensive test suite that exercises all major API patterns using only non-deprecated calls
6. Verified all 17 tests pass with `JULIA_DEPWARN=error`

## Test plan

- [x] All tests pass with `JULIA_DEPWARN=error`
- [x] Runic formatting passes
- [ ] CI passes on Julia 1 / lts / pre

title: AutoSpecialize & NoSpecialize mode JIT recompiling solvers
body:
**Describe the bug 🐞**

I'm trying to construct a benchmark that only uses precompiled solvers and avoids any JIT compilation of the solvers using the specialization levels, however I can't seem to do this. I'm not sure if this is bug or something I'm not doing correctly, can you please advise.

**Minimal Reproducible Example 👇**

```julia
import DifferentialEquations as DE
using SciMLBase

ngroups = 1
function rober!(du, u, p, t)
        k₁, k₂, k₃ = p
        y₁ = @view u[1:ngroups]
        y₂ = @view u[ngroups+1:2*ngroups]
        y₃ = @view u[2*ngroups+1:3*ngroups]
        dy₁ = @view du[1:ngroups]
        dy₂ = @view du[ngroups+1:2*ngroups]
        dy₃ = @view du[2*ngroups+1:3*ngroups]
        dy₁ .= -k₁ .* y₁ .+ k₃ .* y₂ .* y₃
        dy₂ .= k₁ .* y₁ .- k₂ .* y₂ .^2 .- k₃ .* y₂ .* y₃
        dy₃ .= k₂ .* y₂ .^2
        nothing
end

function setup()
        u0 = vcat(ones(ngroups), zeros(2*ngroups))
        p = [0.04, 3e7, 1e4]
        tspan = (0.0, 1e10)
        prob = DE.ODEProblem{true}(rober!, u0, tspan, p)
        return prob
end

setup1 = @elapsed model = setup()
println("Setup time 1: ", setup1)
setup1 = @elapsed model = setup()
println("Setup time 1 (2nd run): ", setup1)

alg1 = DE.FBDF()
solve11 = @elapsed sol1 = DE.solve(model, alg1)
println("solve time 1 (alg1): ", solve11)
solve12 = @elapsed sol1 = DE.solve(model, alg1)
println("solve time 2 (alg1): ", solve12)
alg2 = DE.TRBDF2()
solve13 = @elapsed sol1 = DE.solve(model, alg2)
println("solve time 3 (alg2): ", solve13)
solve14 = @elapsed sol1 = DE.solve(model, alg2)
println("solve time 4 (alg2): ", solve14)
```

```
Setup time 1: 0.063077009
Setup time 1 (2nd run): 2.1841e-5
solve time 1 (alg1): 1.834793159
solve time 2 (alg1): 0.011158691
solve time 3 (alg2): 2.418359262
solve time 4 (alg2): 0.062127387
```

**Expected behavior**

Based on the documentation [here](https://docs.sciml.ai/SciMLBase/stable/interfaces/Problems/#Specialization-Levels) and @ChrisRackauckas comment [here](https://github.com/openjournals/joss-reviews/issues/9384#issuecomment-3816823742) I would expect that autospecialize would use the precompiled solvers and avoid JIT recompilation of the solvers when they are first used in "solve time 1" and "solve time 3", resulting in solve time 1 & 3 to be similar to solve time 2 & 4. Due to the uncertainty of the "auto" nature of this specialization, I have also tried `SciMLBase.NoSpecialize`, which only gives increased JIT compilation time (again contrary to the documentation which indicates that NoSpecialize should give the best compile time performance):

```
Setup time 1: 0.058747097
Setup time 1 (2nd run): 2.2562e-5
solve time 1 (alg1): 6.135955937
solve time 2 (alg1): 0.026723698
solve time 3 (alg2): 3.147232052
solve time 4 (alg2): 0.054692904
```

title: PresetTimeCallback skipped for certain constant lags in DDEs
body: **Describe the bug 🐞** `PresetTimeCallback` is sometimes skipped with certain configurations of constant lags in the DDE setting. I would guess this also affects regular `DiscreteCallback`s, although I don't have a definitive MRE in the case. Possibly related to #1123. **Expected behavior** `PresetTimeCallback` is called no matter the constant lags used. **Minimal Reproducible Example 👇** MRE of two LIF with one-directional coupling. The second LIF should behave like an ODE. ```julia using Revise using Plots, DifferentialEquations using Statistics function lif2_Ndelay!(du, u, h, p, t) u1, u2 = u gL1, EL1, C1, Vth1, I1, gL2, EL2, C2, Vth2, I2, λ, T... = p H = Float64[h(p, t - τ)[2] for τ in T] append!(H, u2) du[1] = (-gL1 * (u1 - EL1) + I1 - λ * (u1 - mean(H))) / C1 du[2] = (-gL2 * (u2 - EL2) + I2) / C2 end threshold1 = ContinuousCallback( (u, t, integrator) -> u[1] - integrator.p[4], (integrator) -> integrator.u[1] = integrator.p[2]) threshold2 = ContinuousCallback( (u, t, integrator) -> u[2] - integrator.p[9], (integrator) -> integrator.u[2] = integrator.p[7]) # Just turning on/off the external current for the 2nd LIF up_Iex2(integrator) = integrator.p[10] = 210.0 down_Iex2(integrator) = integrator.p[10] = 0 current_step_up = PresetTimeCallback([2, 9], up_Iex2) current_step_down = PresetTimeCallback([3, 10], down_Iex2) cb = CallbackSet(threshold1, threshold2, current_step_up, current_step_down) u0 = [-75, -75] tspan = (0.0, 12.0) # p = (gL, EL, C, Vth, I) p1 = [10.0, -75.0, 5.0, -55.0, 100] p2 = [10.0, -75.0, 5.0, -55.0, 0] delays = [0.2, 4] # Contrast to [0.1, 4]! p_both_Ndelay = [p1; p2; [2]; delays] h(p, t) = u0 prob_Ndelay = DDEProblem(lif2_Ndelay!, u0, h, tspan, p_both_Ndelay, callback=cb, constant_lags=delays) sol_Ndelay = solve(prob_Ndelay) plot(sol_Ndelay; xlim=tspan, ylim=(-76, -54)) ``` **Error & Stacktrace ⚠️** There is no real error; it's just that the callback is not called. For example, this is the buggy behaviour (see time 9ms, where the external current should be increased, thus causing a spike in the second LIF, which doesn't happen) On the other hand, when I set the delays to `[0.1, 4]` (or `[0.3, 4]`), I get the correct behaviour **Environment (please complete the following information):** - Output of `using Pkg; Pkg.status()` ```julia Status title: VectorContinuousCallback is skipped
body: **Describe the bug 🐞** The `VectorContinuousCallback` misses when it should be called. Possibly related to #1124. **Expected behavior** When the condition for the callback evaluates to 0, the callback should be called and, in this particular case, it should mutate the state. **Minimal Reproducible Example 👇** Without MRE, we would only be able to help you to a limited extent, and attention to the issue would be limited. to know more about MRE refer to [wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minimal_reproducible_example) and [stackoverflow](https://stackoverflow.com/help/minimal-reproducible-example). ```julia using Revise using RecursiveArrayTools using Plots, DifferentialEquations function rlifN!(dU, U, p, t) gL, EL, C, Vth, Vreset, τ, λ, Iex = p u, v = U.x δu = [uᵢ - uⱼ for uᵢ ∈ u, uⱼ ∈ u] Δu = sum(λ * δu; dims=2) dU.x[1] .= @. (v <= 0) * (-gL * (u - EL) + Iex(t) + Δu) / C dU.x[2] .= @. -(v > 0) end N = 4 cb = VectorContinuousCallback( (out, U, t, integrator) -> out .= U.x[1] .- integrator.p[4], (integrator, idx) -> begin integrator.u.x[1][idx] = integrator.p[5] integrator.u.x[2][idx] = integrator.p[6] end, N ) u0 = ArrayPartition(Float64[ -37.89341270519693 -46.25013154738811 -39.70532952550151 -44.8639480491058 ], zeros(N)) tspan = (0.0, 32.0) Iex(t) = 500 * (sin(2π * 0.05 * t - π / 2) + 1) λ = zeros(N, N) # p = (gL, EL, C, Vth, Vreset, τ, λ, Iex) p = (12.5, -50.0, 9.7, -10.0, -60.0, 3, λ, Iex) prob = ODEProblem(rlifN!, u0, tspan, p, callback=cb) sol = solve(prob) begin plot(sol; xlim=tspan, ylim=(-62, 3), legend=:left) hline!([p[4]], label="Threshold", linestyle=:dash, color=:red) end ``` **Error & Stacktrace ⚠️** There is no real error; it's just that the callback is not called. For example, this is the buggy behaviour (see time ~29 ms) - it should never go over the threshold -10. title: saveat bug when solving an SDE with a ContinuousCallback
body:
I am solving a stochastic differential equation with a `ContinuousCallback`. Every time the `ContinuousCallback` is activated, I modify my state vector discontinuously.

All the randomness comes from a phase, which follows a simple Wiener process, i.e., the phase is not coupled to the remaining variables of the differential equation. Here is a somewhat minimal example:

```
using StochasticDiffEq
using DiffEqCallbacks
using Random

α = 1.0
β = 1.0
σφ = 0.5

u₀ = [0.5, 0.0]
tspan = (0.0, 10.0)

# Drift
function f(u, p, t)
    A, φ = u
    return [
        α * A * cos(φ),  # amplitude coupled to phase
        0.0              # phase has no drift
    ]
end

# Diffusion
function g(u, p, t)
    A, φ = u
    return [
        β * A,
        σφ       # Wiener process for phase
    ]
end

prob = SDEProblem(f, g, u₀, tspan)

rng = MersenneTwister(123)

# Random threshold for the amplitude u[1]
threshold = Ref(rand(rng, 0.2:0.001:1.0))

# Trigger when amplitude crosses the threshold
condition(u, t, integrator) = u[1] - threshold[]

# Reset rule
function affect!(integrator)
    integrator.u[1] *= 2.0
    threshold[] = rand(rng, 0.2:0.001:1.0)
end

cb = ContinuousCallback(condition, affect!;)

sol = solve(
    prob,
    SRIW1(),
    seed = 123,
    abstol = 1e-2,
    reltol = 1e-2,
    maxiters = Int(1e10),
    saveat = 0.01,
    callback = cb
)

# Plot sol[2,:]
```


I sometimes observe a discontinuous change in the phase when the ContinuousCallback is activated. When I set saveat = [], the spikes vanish. Unfortunately I cannot upload any plots currently, but here is a link to the julia Forum where I asked a question that was answered by @ChrisRackauckas: https://discourse.julialang.org/t/solving-an-sde-with-a-continuous-callback/135180/6


DifferentialEquations v7.17.0
StochasticDiffEq v6.87.0
DiffEqCallbacks v4.12.0

julia version 1.12.1

title: [CI Issue] Spell Check consistently failing on false positives in SVG file
body:
## Summary

The Spell Check CI job is consistently failing on all PRs due to false positives in an auto-generated SVG file.

## Which CI job failed

**Spell Check with Typos** - Fails in ~7 seconds on every PR

## Error Details

The spell checker (`crate-ci/typos`) is flagging the identifier `daa` in `./assets/DifferentialEquations_Example.svg` as a typo (suggesting it should be "data"). However, this is not a typo - it's part of auto-generated SVG element IDs like `m2daa2affb1`.

**Affected locations in SVG:** Lines 50, 53, 97, 146, 185, 209, 4101, 4126, 4151, 4176

Example from the SVG:
\`\`\`xml
<defs>
 <path d="..." id="m2daa2affb1" style="stroke:#000000;"/>
</defs>
<use style="stroke:#000000;" x="15.964646" xlink:href="#m2daa2affb1" y="15.754646"/>
\`\`\`

## Root Cause

The spell check workflow (`.github/workflows/SpellCheck.yml`) uses `crate-ci/typos@v1.18.0` which doesn't exclude binary/generated files by default. The `.typos.toml` configuration doesn't currently exclude SVG files or whitelist the `daa` identifier pattern.

## Recent History

- Spell check was added in PR #1098 (merged 2025-07-29)
- Recent merged PRs #1117 and #1116 both had spell check failures but were merged anyway
- This suggests the check is not currently required for merging, but the consistent failures create noise

## Suggested Fix

Add to `.typos.toml`:

\`\`\`toml
[files]
extend-exclude = ["*.svg", "*.png"]
\`\`\`

OR add the false positive to the dictionary:

\`\`\`toml
[default.extend-words]
daa = "daa"
\`\`\`

The first option (excluding SVG files) is cleaner since SVG files are typically auto-generated and shouldn't need spell checking.

## Related Links

- Failed CI run: https://github.com/SciML/DifferentialEquations.jl/actions/runs/20796520557/job/59731349664
- Health check PR: https://github.com/SciML/DifferentialEquations.jl/pull/1119

title: Quantum Simulations dissipate over time across all solvers
body:
**Describe the bug 🐞**

I tried simulating a quantum system using both QuantumToolbox.jl and QuantumOptics.jl. In both cases I get a similar behavior - for some states I get dissipation, and for other I get no time evolution (expected). I am opening the issue here as both libraries use DifferentialEquations.jl to integrate the schrodinger equation.

Doing the same simulation in python using qutip returns the correct behavior.

**Expected behavior**

I expect the overlap of each state with itself to remain constant in time, but for some reason we get dissipation.

**Minimal Reproducible Example 👇**

QuantumToolbox:

```julia
using QuantumToolbox, CairoMakie, DifferentialEquations

begin 
	Nr = 30
	Nt = 3
	const a = tensor(destroy(Nt), qeye(Nr))
	const c = tensor(qeye(Nt), destroy(Nr))
	const GHz = 2π;
	const MHz = 1e-3GHz;
	const η = 255MHz;
	const ωa = 5.0GHz;
	const ν = 5.6GHz;
	const g = 4MHz
end;

H0 = ωa * a' * a + ν * c' * c - η/2 * a' * a' * a * a + g * (a' * c + c' * a);
Hrot = (ν + (g^2/(ν - ωa))) * (a' * a + c' * c);
H₀ = H0 - Hrot;

energies, states = eigenstates(H₀);

const bare_states = [
	tensor(basis(Nt, 0), basis(Nr, 0)),
	tensor(basis(Nt, 1), basis(Nr, 0)),
	tensor(basis(Nt, 0), basis(Nr, 1)),
	tensor(basis(Nt, 1), basis(Nr, 1)),
];

begin
	logical_states = []
	for state in bare_states
		overlaps = [abs2(state' * s) for s in states]
		push!(logical_states, states[argmax(overlaps)])
	end
end

# using the default solver
let	fig = Figure(; size=(800, 800))
	
	ax = Axis(fig[1, 1],
	    xlabel="Time [ns]",
	    ylabel="Overlap",
	)

	Tgate = 1500.0
	tlist = -50.0:0.01Tgate:1.2Tgate
	sesol = sesolve(H₀, logical_states[2], tlist, progress_bar=false)
	for state in states
		pop = [abs2(state' * s) for s in sesol.states]
		if maximum(pop) > 1e-15
			scatter!(ax, tlist, pop, label="Using sesolve")
		end
	end
	manual_prop = zero(tlist)
	st = logical_states[2]
	for (i, t) in enumerate(tlist)
		st = exp(-1.0im * t * H₀) * st
		manual_prop[i] = abs2(logical_states[2]' * st)
	end

	scatter!(ax, tlist, manual_prop, label="Manual Propogation")
	axislegend(ax)
	fig
end

# changing the solver

let	fig = Figure(; size=(800, 800))
	
	ax = Axis(fig[1, 1],
	    xlabel="Time [ns]",
	    ylabel="Overlap",
	)

	Tgate = 1500.0
	tlist = -50.0:0.01Tgate:1.2Tgate
	sesol = sesolve(H₀, logical_states[2], tlist, progress_bar=false, alg=Vern9())
	for state in states
		pop = [abs2(state' * s) for s in sesol.states]
		if maximum(pop) > 1e-15
			scatter!(ax, tlist, pop, label="Using sesolve")
		end
	end
	manual_prop = zero(tlist)
	st = logical_states[2]
	for (i, t) in enumerate(tlist)
		st = exp(-1.0im * t * H₀) * st
		manual_prop[i] = abs2(logical_states[2]' * st)
	end

	scatter!(ax, tlist, manual_prop, label="Manual Propogation")
	axislegend(ax)
	fig
end
```

**Error & Stacktrace ⚠️**

When running the plots, you will see a straight line for the manual calculation (correct result) and a line with a downward slope for the simulation (incorrect).

body:
Bumps [actions/checkout](https://github.com/actions/checkout) from 4 to 6.
Release notes

Sourced from actions/checkout's releases.

v6.0.0

What's Changed

  • Update README to include Node.js 24 support details and requirements by @​salmanmkc in actions/checkout#2248
  • Persist creds to a separate file by @​ericsciple in actions/checkout#2286
  • v6-beta by @​ericsciple in actions/checkout#2298
  • update readme/changelog for v6 by @​ericsciple in actions/checkout#2311

Full Changelog: https://github.com/actions/checkout/compare/v5.0.0...v6.0.0

v6-beta

What's Changed

Updated persist-credentials to store the credentials under $RUNNER_TEMP instead of directly in the local git config.

This requires a minimum Actions Runner version of v2.329.0 to access the persisted credentials for Docker container action scenarios.

v5.0.1

What's Changed

  • Port v6 cleanup to v5 by @​ericsciple in actions/checkout#2301

Full Changelog: https://github.com/actions/checkout/compare/v5...v5.0.1

What's Changed

  • Prepare v5.0.0 release by @​salmanmkc in actions/checkout#2238

⚠️ Minimum Compatible Runner Version

v2.327.1
Release Notes

Make sure your runner is updated to this version or newer to use this release.

title: Linsolve error getting forward-mode gradient of stiff ODE w.r.t. ComponentArray parameters
body:
**Describe the bug 🐞**

Attempting to obtain a gradient w.r.t. a component array of parameters using ForwardDiff fails during the ODE solve for stiff problems.

**Expected behavior**

Gradient is returned properly.

**Minimal Reproducible Example 👇**

```julia
using ComponentArrays, DifferentialEquations, ForwardDiff


function myode!(du, u, p, t)
    #van der pol oscillator for easy stiff/nonstiff testing
    @views a = u.a
    @views b = u.b

    @views da = du.a
    @views db = du.b

    p_a = p.a
    p_b = p.b

    @. da = p_a*b
    @. db = p_b*(1-a^2)*b-a

end


u0 = ComponentArray(a = rand(2), b = zeros(2))

#stiff parameters
ps = ComponentArray(a = 1.0, b = 10000)

prob = ODEProblem(myode!, u0, (0.0, 10000.0), ps)



@time refsol = solve(prob, saveat=0.1);

function lossfn(ps)
    newprob =  remake(prob, p=ps)
    sol = solve(newprob, TRBDF2(), saveat=0.1)
    loss = sum(abs2, stack(refsol.u) .- stack(sol.u))
end

#still stiff, but not the same as reference
testps = ComponentArray(a = 1.0, b = 1000)

#works fine
@time lossfn(testps)

#throws error
@time ForwardDiff.gradient(lossfn, testps)
```

title: SplitODEProblem is using numerical differentiation even when analytical jacobian vector product is provided with a Krylov solver.
body:
**Describe the bug 🐞**

Semilinear ODE (SplitODEProblem) is using numerical differentiation even when analytical jacobian-vector-product of the implicit functio is provided and the implicit stage is configured to be solved with a matrix-free Krylov method. 

In the MRE I have restricted the type to a Vector{Float64}, so that if any Dual is passed it will error. And we can see that a Dual is being passed from the Stacktrace. 

**Expected behavior**

Use analytical jacobian-vector-product function that is provided. Do not perform any numerical differentiation. 

**Minimal Reproducible Example 👇**

```julia
using OrdinaryDiffEq
import LinearSolve as LS

function f1!(du::Vector{Float64}, u, p, t)
	@. du .= -0.5u
	return nothing
end

function jvp_f1!(Jv::Vector{Float64}, v, u, p, t)
	@. Jv .= -0.5v
	return nothing
end

function f2!(du::Vector{Float64}, u, p, t)
	@. du .= 0.1u^2
	return nothing
end

f = SplitFunction(f1!, f2!, jvp = jvp_f1!)
prob = SplitODEProblem(f, [1.0], (0.0, 10.0))

sol = solve(prob, KenCarp4(linsolve = LS.KrylovJL_GMRES()))
```

title: Solving DAE in mass matrix form requires an enormus amount of memory
body:
**Describe the bug 🐞**

As the title says, DAE solve takes a lot memory. For eg in this MRE, a 65,000 unknown problem, with a 0.5 MB vector and 7 MB jacobian, it takes over 20GB of memory before exiting due to running out of memory. 
The solve completes for sparser discretization, albeit still taking a lot of memory. 

I also made a [post on discourse](https://discourse.julialang.org/t/dae-solve-asking-for-an-unreasonable-amount-of-memory/133051/5) about this, where I tried a few thing to eliminate memory usage like, analytical jacobian, or Krylov matrix free method for Jacobian vector solve, not saving solution, etc. 

**Expected behavior**

I expect it to take memory of O(n). 

**Minimal Reproducible Example 👇**

```julia
using LinearAlgebra: LinearAlgebra
import DifferentialEquations as DE
import SparseArrays: SparseArrays
using SparseConnectivityTracer: SparseConnectivityTracer
using ADTypes: ADTypes
using ProgressLogging

# Landau Khalatnikov equation with memory effect
"""
(dP/dt)  = -Γ (α P + β P^3 + γ = P^5 - g11 ∇²P + ∇ϕ)
(dϕ/dt) = ∇^2ϕ - ∇ ⋅ P 
"""

function f!(du, u, p, t)
	α, β, γ, g, Γ, Nx, Ny, Δx, Δy, ϵ = p
	Δx2, Δy2                         = Δx^2, Δy^2
	len_u                            = length(u)

	P  = reshape(view(u, 1:Ny*Nx), Ny, Nx)
	ϕ  = reshape(view(u, (Ny*Nx+1):len_u), Ny, Nx)
	dP = reshape(view(du, 1:Ny*Nx), Ny, Nx)
	dϕ = reshape(view(du, (Ny*Nx+1):len_u), Ny, Nx)

	for j in 1:Ny, i in 1:Nx
		jm1, jp1 = j - 1, j + 1
		im1, ip1 = i - 1, i + 1
		jm1 = jm1 < 1 ? 1 : jm1
		jp1 = jp1 > Ny ? Ny : jp1
		im1 = im1 < 1 ? 1 : im1
		ip1 = ip1 > Nx ? Nx : ip1

		∇²P = (P[j, ip1] - 2P[j, i] + P[j, im1]) / Δx2 +
			  (P[jp1, i] - 2P[j, i] + P[jm1, i]) / Δy2

		∇yϕ = (ϕ[jp1, i] - ϕ[jm1, i]) / (2 * Δy)

		dP[j, i] = -Γ * (α * P[j, i] + β * P[j, i]^3 + γ * P[j, i]^5 - g * ∇²P + ∇yϕ)

		dϕ[j, i] = ϵ * (ϕ[j, ip1] - 2ϕ[j, i] + ϕ[j, im1]) / Δx2 +
				   ϵ * (ϕ[jp1, i] - 2ϕ[j, i] + ϕ[jm1, i]) / Δy2 -
				   (P[jp1, i] - P[jm1, i]) / (2 * Δy)
	end
	return nothing
end

function main()
	Nx = 256 # 40
	Ny = 128 # 20
	P = rand(Ny, Nx)
	ϕ = rand(Ny, Nx)
	Lx = 40.0
	Ly = 20.0

	α, β, γ = -2.5, 60.0, 150.0
	Δx, Δy = Lx / (Nx - 1), Ly / (Ny - 1)
	Γ = 1.0e6
	g = 1.0
	ϵ = 24.0 * 8.854e-12 * 1e9

	p = (α, β, γ, g, Γ, Nx, Ny, Δx, Δy, ϵ)
	u0 = vcat(P[:], ϕ[:])
	du0 = similar(u0)

	M = LinearAlgebra.Diagonal(vcat(ones(Ny * Nx), zeros(Ny * Nx)))

	detector = SparseConnectivityTracer.TracerSparsityDetector()
	du0 = copy(u0)

	jac_sparsity = ADTypes.jacobian_sparsity(
		(du, u) -> f!(du, u, p, 0.0), du0, u0, detector)

	jac = float.(jac_sparsity)

	usize = Base.summarysize(u0) / 1024^2
	jacsize = Base.summarysize(jac) / 1024^2


	println("Unknkowns : $(length(u0))") # 65536
	println("u_size    : $usize MB") # 0.5 MB 
	println("jac_size  : $jacsize MB") # 7.47 MB


	ode_f = DE.ODEFunction(f!; jac_prototype = jac, mass_matrix = M)
	prob = DE.ODEProblem(ode_f, u0, (0.0, 1e7), p)

	@elapsed tsol = sol = DE.solve(prob, DE.FBDF(), save_everystep = false, saveat = Float64[], progress = true)
	println("Time taken for solve: $tsol seconds")
end

main()
```

**Error & Stacktrace ⚠️**
This takes a huge amount of memory over 20 GB and then crashes due to OOM. I don't know to check memory form inside julia. Putting summarysize(Main) inside the function just slowed down everything. So here is the screenshot of memory usage from my OS.

## Summary
This PR removes the default SDE algorithm selection from DifferentialEquations.jl, as it has been moved to StochasticDiffEq.jl.

Closes #1086 (partial - for SDE portion)

This is part of the ongoing effort to modularize DifferentialEquations.jl by moving default solver logic to their respective packages (see #1086). The SDE default algorithm is now handled directly in StochasticDiffEq.jl via `__init` and `__solve` dispatches when no algorithm is specified.

## Related PRs

## Breaking Changes
None - this is purely an internal refactoring. The user-facing API remains unchanged. Users can still call `solve(sde_problem)` without specifying an algorithm and the appropriate default will be selected by StochasticDiffEq.jl.

title: IMEXBDF example is wrong
body:
The example shown on https://docs.sciml.ai/DiffEqDocs/stable/api/ordinarydiffeq/imex/IMEXBDF/#IMEX-Multistep-Methods is wrong.

As the documentation on that page states: "These methods require a SplitODEProblem formulation". However, the example below does not do that; it only contains the line
```
prob = ODEProblem(lorenz!, u0, tspan)
```
The example does not make sense since there is only a single RHS function defined (`lorenz!`) instead of two separate ones. The main point of IMEX methods is to split the RHS into two separate ones.

title: Initialize line split fixes following Catalyst.jl PR #1306
body:
## Summary

Initialize fixing unnecessary line splits in Julia code following the guidelines established in [Catalyst.jl PR #1306](https://github.com/SciML/Catalyst.jl/pull/1306). This PR sets up the framework for improving code readability by consolidating short expressions that are unnecessarily split across multiple lines.

## Background

These formatting issues are being addressed upstream in [JuliaFormatter.jl PR #934](https://github.com/domluna/JuliaFormatter.jl/pull/934), which implements algorithmic fixes to prevent these unnecessary line splits. However, since that PR is not yet merged, manual fixes are needed in the meantime to improve code readability.

## Current Status

This PR creates the branch and initial framework. The repository appears to have mostly well-formatted code with justified line splits for complex function signatures.

## Note

This is part of a systematic effort to apply the same formatting improvements across 10+ SciML repositories following the successful implementation in JumpProcesses.jl, OrdinaryDiffEq.jl, LinearSolve.jl, NonlinearSolve.jl, and ModelingToolkit.jl.

title: Non-autonomous Linear ODE solver example fails
body:
Describe the bug 🐞
Hi folks, following up on https://github.com/SciML/SciMLOperators.jl/issues/287, since I'm not sure where the right place to post this is.

Thanks for the package! I'm currently trying to build off of the examples in the docs for the Non-autonomous Linear ODE solvers, but I'm running into type conversion errors when using the SciML MatrixOperator.

Minimal Reproducible Example 👇

using OrdinaryDiffEq, StaticArrays, SciMLOperators
function update_func(A, u, p, t)
    A[1, 1] = cos(t)
    A[2, 1] = sin(t)
    A[1, 2] = -sin(t)
    A[2, 2] = cos(t)
end
A = SciMLOperators.MatrixOperator(ones(2, 2), update_func = update_func)
prob = ODEProblem(A, ones(2), (1.0, 6.0))
sol = solve(prob, MagnusGL6(), dt = 1 / 10)

Error & Stacktrace ⚠️

title: set_u! not respected on first time step of Euler()
body:
**Describe the bug 🐞**

set_u! does not work when applied to the first time step. It does update the values of u in the integrator but the derivative is not reevaluated on the new state. This looks to only apply for the Euler() algorithm.

**Expected behavior**

set_u! should mark the derivative as having changed, so the first step should lead to an increase in u[1] since u[2] is positive.

**Minimal Reproducible Example 👇**
```julia
using DifferentialEquations
function f!(du, u, p, t)
    x, y = u
    du[1] = y
    du[2] = 0
end

prob1 = ODEProblem(f!, [4.0,-1.0], (0.0,1.0))

int = init(prob1, Euler(); dt=0.002, adaptive=false, save_everystep=false)
println("Failing version: Change u[2] to 2 before the first step")
@show (int.t,int.u)
println("Change u[2] here")
set_u!(int, [4.0, 2.0])
@show (int.t,int.u)
step!(int)
@show (int.t,int.u)
println("u[1] decreased but should have increased")
step!(int)
@show (int.t,int.u)
println("Later steps work fine")
println()

int = init(prob1, Euler(); dt=0.002, adaptive=false, save_everystep=false)
println("Working version: Change u[2] to 2 after the first step")
@show (int.t,int.u)
step!(int)
@show (int.t,int.u)
println("Change u[2] here")
set_u!(int, [4.0, 2.0])
@show (int.t,int.u)
println("This time u[1] didn't decrease because we only used set_u! after the first step")
step!(int)
@show (int.t,int.u)
step!(int)
@show (int.t,int.u)
```

(int.t, int.u) = (0.0, [4.0, -1.0])
Change u[2] here

(int.t, int.u) = (0.002, [3.998, 2.0])
u[1] decreased but should have increased
(int.t, int.u) = (0.004, [4.002, 2.0])
Later steps work fine

Working version: Change u[2] to 2 after the first step
(int.t, int.u) = (0.0, [4.0, -1.0])
(int.t, int.u) = (0.002, [3.998, -1.0])
Change u[2] here
(int.t, int.u) = (0.002, [4.0, 2.0])
This time u[1] didn't decrease because we only used set_u! after the first step
(int.t, int.u) = (0.004, [4.004, 2.0])
(int.t, int.u) = (0.006, [4.007999999999999, 2.0])
(0.006, [4.007999999999999, 2.0])
```

title: QNDF gets stuck when solving for a steady state to high tolerances
body:
**Describe the bug 🐞**

I am solving a SteadyState ODE problem with the DynamicSS solver using QNDF and the solver gets stuck when setting both abstol and reltol very small. The reason why I think this is a bug and not just the system taking a long time is that I suspect the algorithm gets stuck within a single QNDF step (as opposed to just taking many steps) meaning there is no way to interrupt it that I could find, and perhaps this seems like something that should not happen. I don't know how to debug this enough to give a precise reason for what I experience however the general observations are as follow:
- I've implemented a discrete callback that checks real time at each iteration and will exit after a set interval however this never triggers suggesting QNDF get stuck in the middle of one iteration.
- The solver cannot be interrupted, trying Control-C makes julia fail entirely - usually I just get back to the repl.
- QNDF works when abstol=reltol=1000\*eps() and takes ~0.01s to solve the problem but changing them to 100\*eps() makes it hang. I realize this might just be its limit but this seems like an extreme case, I have had this solver ran for over 2 days on a cluster.
- TRBDF2 works despite it usually being slower - at the 1000\*eps() option it takes ~0.08s, but unlike QNDF it works even at 100\*eps().
- In addition if I really push TRBDF2 beyond reason setting tolerances to eps() / 100, it still triggers my timer and the solver will exit after the specified time without a solution.

**Expected behavior**

I am aware this is a tricky subject but I suppose I would like something similar to how TRBDF2 works and make sure QNDF at least occasionally will make an iteration. On a separate note, in general having a real time limit for solvers would be great in my opinion as a solver getting stuck is sometimes unavoidable and hence having a way to recover from that would be great!

**Minimal Reproducible Example 👇**

This is fairly difficult as the problem is part of a growing codebase and relies on the parameters being a custom struct. However, I can point to a github with a notebook containing one, hopefully this should be easy to run! (Besides waiting 10min for the dependencies to install and precompile)
THe github is: https://github.com/kockahonza/SSMC/tree/debug_qndf_differentialequations with the notebook containing a MWE being here: https://github.com/kockahonza/SSMC/blob/debug_qndf_differentialequations/notebooks/rg_unstructured.ipynb .

title: Lie group solver documentation
body:
Most of the examples on this page have completely wrong output: https://docs.sciml.ai/DiffEqDocs/stable/solvers/nonautonomous_linear_ode/

The reason is that the MatrixOperator is passed update_func (should be returning a new matrix), but the update_func used instead mutates the matrix.

title: Infinite loop when locating successive events during backward integration
body:
**Describe the bug 🐞**

During a **backward** ODE integration with event callback, when the condition crosses 0 twice successively, the solver fails to locate the second crossing and instead goes back to the first occurence. This either causes an infinite loop or an out of step interpolation `ERROR: LoadError: Current interpolant only works between tprev and t`.

In the Minimal Reproducible Example below, the second crossing happens within one time step of the first, but in my original (more complex) code the second crossing happens a few steps after the first.
I have put part of the output of `println()` in the stacktrace section.

**Expected behavior**

The ODE solver should properly locate the second crossing. Everything works fine when integrating forward so this should be possible.

**Minimal Reproducible Example 👇**

Locating the roots of `cos(t) + 0.9` on a dummy ODE. This produce an infinite loop

```julia
using OrdinaryDiffEq
using StaticArrays

cb = ContinuousCallback(
    (y, t, integrator) -> (println("condition;", integrator.tprev, ";", t, ";", cos(t) + 0.9); cos(t) + 0.9),
    integrator -> println("Up:   t=", integrator.t),
    integrator -> println("Down: t=", integrator.t)
)

problem = ODEProblem{false,SciMLBase.FullSpecialize}(
    (y, p, t) -> SA[1.0],
    SA[0.0], (0, -10π),
    callback=cb,
    dtmax=1.0
)

solve(problem, DP5())
```

**Error & Stacktrace ⚠️**
Infinite loop output :
